what: Two independently driven joints position the end of an 80 mm / 64 mm serial arm. Two independently driven joints position the tip. Compare measured coordinates with the 80 mm / 64 mm serial-arm equations.
try: Compare the two elbow postures near the same tip position.
Stop and change one joint slightly; watch how both tip coordinates change.
why: The elbow is carried by the shoulder. Its angle adds to the shoulder angle when calculating the forearm direction. Two different joint configurations can reach nearly the same point.
matters: Robot arms must solve geometry as well as control motor angles.
question: Do shoulder and elbow angles act in the same fixed frame?
answer: No. The elbow’s reference frame rotates with the shoulder, so the forearm uses the sum of the two angles.
further: Predict what happens near a fully extended posture.
Compare position with orientation: this arm does not independently set a tool angle.
formula:
x = 80 cos(A) + 64 cos(A+B)
y = 80 sin(A) + 64 sin(A+B)  [mm]
